claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding are initially protective.
High-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
Cr–Zr interdiffusion produces deleterious intermetallic compounds.
A 50–100 nm interfacial CrN layer will significantly reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
A 50–100 nm interfacial CrN layer will improve the overall durability of the Cr coating relative to an unmodified Cr-coated control.
A 50–100 nm interfacial CrN layer will improve oxidation resistance relative to an unmodified Cr-coated control.
The proposed CrN-modified coating will remain protective in subcritical water at approximately 350°C for up to several thousand hours.
The proposed CrN-modified coating will remain protective in steam at approximately 1000°C for up to one hour.
A continuous, adherent CrN layer physically interrupts direct contact between the zirconium substrate and elemental Cr coating.
Interrupting direct Zr–Cr contact with CrN limits atomic diffusion across the interface.
CrN is refractory under the proposed service conditions.
CrN has low mutual solubility with both zirconium and chromium.
The CrN layer provides a kinetically sluggish diffusion path for interfacial element transport.
CrN provides enhanced oxidation resistance that helps preserve the integrity of the overlying Cr coating.
Post-deposition annealing will enhance adhesion and uniformity of the CrN barrier.
Defects or discontinuities in the CrN layer could compromise its diffusion-blocking efficacy.
Defects or discontinuities in the CrN layer could compromise oxidation resistance.
